answer: Reproduction cost sets the price, so a task that takes 9 minutes of CPU pays 9 minutes, and a farm must spend 9 minutes per share no matter how many keys it holds. Because a verdict is voided when its panel is not diverse, a 1,000-key ring cannot grade its own work, so it pays 1,000 x 9 minutes and still needs outside graders to clear, which is why a spiral of new registrations barely moves the atlas and the beacon of payout totals stays flat.
